title: Expression of CGRP in the Trigeminal Ganglion and Its Effect on the Polarization of Macrophages in Rats with Temporomand

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: "primary headaches, including migraines and TMD, often involve the trigeminal nervous system in their pathogenesis." TMD (temporomandibular disorder) is not a primary headache disorder; it is a musculoskeletal/orofacial pain disorder. Classifying TMD as a primary headache is factually wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract vs Results: trigeminal ganglion CD86+ macrophage time course
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states that "within 24 h of inducing temporomandibular arthritis using CFA, there was a significant surge in CD86 positive macrophages within the ganglion." However, the Results section reports for TG CD86-positive macrophages on days 1, 3, 7, and 14: "p = 0.7376, p = 0.1193, p < 0.0001, and p < 0.0001, respectively." The day-1 p-value of 0.7376 does not indicate a significant surge within 24 h, directly contradicting the abstract.

The text states that HWT "was notably reduced on days 1, 3, 7, and 14 post-injection when compared to controls (p = 0.2747, p = 0.0102, p = 0.0017, and p = 0.3946, respectively)." The day-1 p-value of 0.2747 and day-14 p-value of 0.3946 are not statistically significant, so the claim that HWT was notably reduced on all four time points is unsupported.

The Results state: "Notably, CD86-positive M1 macrophages significantly increased one day after CFA treatment, peaking at day 7 (Fig. 5B)." But the corresponding p-values are reported as "p = 0.6672, p = 0.1276, p < 0.0001, p = 0.0033, respectively" for days 1, 3, 7, and 14. A day-1 p-value of 0.6672 is not significant, so the claim of a significant increase at one day is false.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, effect of TG injection of CGRP/CGRP8-37 on CD86 macrophages
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says: "CD86-positive macrophages were significantly increased and decreased, respectively (p < 0.001 and p = 0.1939, respectively)." A p-value of 0.1939 for the CGRP condition is not statistically significant, so describing the decrease as significant is unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, effect of CGRP8-37 on M2 polarization in TG
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that CGRP8-37 "impeded this M2 polarization" and reports CD206-positive macrophage results as "p = 0.6133 and p = 0.0403, respectively." The p-value of 0.6133 for CGRP8-37 indicates no significant change in CD206-positive M2 macrophages, contradicting the claim that CGRP8-37 impeded M2 polarization.

The Methods list "CGRP (CST, ab81887, 1:1000)" as a Cell Signaling Technology antibody. Catalog number ab81887 is an Abcam anti-CGRP antibody, not a CST product. The vendor/antibody attribution is inconsistent.

The paper uses complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) to induce "temporomandibular arthritis," but the keywords include "Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis," and the Introduction refers to "the chronic pain phase of OA." CFA-induced arthritis is an inflammatory/immune-driven arthritis model, not a standard osteoarthritis (OA) model. The nomenclature conflates inflammatory arthritis with osteoarthritis.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, behavioral effect of CGRP injection on HWT
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says CGRP injection without antagonist "led to decreased HWT at these same time points compared to the saline group (p = 0.0024, p = 0.3595, p = 0.0436, respectively)." The day-3 p-value of 0.3595 is not significant, so the statement that CGRP decreased HWT at all the same time points is not fully supported.
